items.title: Show HN: I built an interactive visual playground for interaction nets
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN!
I built a tool to make it easy to explore interaction nets visually in the browser.
Interaction nets are a model of computation based on local graph rewriting. They allow for deterministic, massively parallel evaluation without the variable-binding overhead of traditional lambda calculus.
I've been thinking about interaction nets for a while and realised that I just didn't have a good intuition for them. I found it hard to visualise how they worked, what sorts of programs you can express

(Too many channels, easy to lose things, distracted from actual work.) I set out to build a platform that would encourage asynchronous communication with an option to break glass if needed. items.title: Show HN: A tool to optimize AI model cost without benchmark score trade-offs
items.contentSnippet:
I created this page to apply data envelopment analysis to find the Pareto frontier of cost and benchmark scores. The goal is to identify the cheapest model or a theoretical blend of models applied to tasks that meets the same benchmark scores as your selected model. This is based on a 2022 paper I coauthored. Benchmark sources include Artificial Analysis, ToneBench, Hermes3000 and Slidely, from September–October 2026.
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50351277
